dedupe_keys.name: evaluation of deep reinforcement learning for restoration in optical networks

description: Carlos Hernandez and colleagues document this resource in the B5G-OPEN community. A trained reinforcement-learning agent autonomously restores optical lightpaths after a link failure. It is compared with heuristic algorithms under different traffic loads and failure durations. Coverage is the reported network-restoration evaluation; the short abstract omits topology, training procedure and quantitative superiority bounds. The model represents a completed algorithm experiment and does not imply that an operator deployed the controller. A separate routing/provisioning model has a different decision trigger and is not merged by topic alone. Zenodo provides the descriptive publication with open access; its stated licence is cc-by-4.0. Its publication licence does not establish a code licence or source-code availability. A limitation is that the native metadata do not establish all implementation settings, uncertainty bounds or independent reproducibility. Only descriptive metadata were inspected. Related records and companion papers retain their source-defined roles; they do not imply independent measurements. The model supports restoration decisions following optical-link failure.
